extraction.name: SciQ
extraction.description: A dataset of 13.7K multiple choice science exam questions.
extraction.creator: Johannes Welbl, Nelson F. Liu, Matt Gardner
extraction.rai:dataCollection: A two-step process: first presenting a set of candidate passages to a crowd worker to choose one and ask a question about it. Second, another worker takes the question and answer and produces three distractors, aided by a model trained to predict good answer distractors.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Science study textbooks from various online learning resources, including CK-12 and OpenStax. The books are about biology, chemistry, earth science and physics and span elementary level to college introductory material.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A rule-based document filter model classified individual sentences and accepted a paragraph if a minimum number of sentences was accepted. Sentences were filtered out based on 15 lexical, grammatical, pragmatical and complexity based rules (e.g., if they were a question, had no verb phrase, contained modal verbs, etc.).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Workers were instructed to judge whether the question could appear in a school science exam, select up to two of the six suggested distractors, and write at least one distractor by themselves such that there is a total of three.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Crowd workers found the predicted distractors good enough to include in the final question around half of the time, resulting in 36.1% of the distractors in the final dataset being generated by the model. A qualitative evaluation showed humans identified the real science exam question versus the crowdsourced question in only 55% of cases, falling below the significance level of p=0.05.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers with Master's status.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Rule-based document filter model, Random forest classifier for distractor prediction
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: A small percentage of the passages were obtained from unreleasable texts, so the direct answer version of SciQ is slightly smaller than the multiple choice version.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation. Useful for studying reading comprehension models in medium-data settings and as additional training data to improve model performance on real science exams.
